picks.title: First AI-driven telescope opens a new era of stargazing
picks.excerpt: Northwestern, University of Chicago and Fermilab researchers deployed the first AI system that decides where a telescope points, scheduling Dark Energy Camera observations on the Blanco 4-meter telescope and adapting in real time to weather and seeing.
picks.rationale: First time an AI holds the pointing decision on a major telescope — observation scheduling stops being a human queue and becomes a live control loop.

picks.title: Cleveland Clinic and IBM researchers create quantum machine learning framework to predict neoantigen immune response
picks.excerpt: Cleveland Clinic and IBM researchers built Q-CHIPP, a quantum machine learning framework that beats classical methods at predicting which tumor mutations trigger an immune response under data-limited conditions.
picks.rationale: A rare concrete claim of quantum ML advantage where it should matter most — small, expensive biological datasets rather than benchmark-scale data.

picks.title: AI framework rooted in cognitive science plans more efficiently at a fraction of the energy
picks.excerpt: A cognitive-science-inspired AI framework built on cognitive maps solves planning problems more efficiently and with far lower energy use than conventional deep neural networks.
picks.rationale: Argues the planning win comes from borrowing the brain's cognitive-map representation rather than from scaling — a different lever than bigger models.

picks.title: US National Science Foundation putting $380 million into building self-driving labs
picks.excerpt: The US National Science Foundation is putting $380 million into AI-enabled autonomous laboratories, including a $20 million NC State-led 'self-driving' chemistry lab aimed at cutting molecular discovery from years to weeks.
picks.rationale: National-scale funding turns autonomous labs from demos into standing infrastructure, resetting the baseline for how discovery work gets staffed and run.

picks.title: They changed their minds on AI. Who's next?
picks.excerpt: Schrodinger CEO Ramy Farid, a longtime physics-based-simulation partisan in drug design, explains what changed his mind about where machine learning now fits in computational discovery.
picks.rationale: A leading physics-first holdout publicly redrawing the line between simulation and ML — the clearest signal yet of where computational drug design settles.
